name: LA-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Speaker Mike Johnson's incumbency and national profile in an R+17 district
Overwhelming money advantage: $21M raised and $9.6M on hand versus under $300K for each Democrat
Prediction markets price Johnson at roughly 94% to win
No public polling and no expert ratings flag the race as competitive
model.rationale: The district's strong Republican lean, Johnson's Speaker-level fundraising and visibility, and markets pricing his win odds near 94% leave Democrats with no realistic path; the expected margin sits in the high teens for Republicans.
model.watch: A major national Democratic wave or an unexpected scandal involving Johnson could narrow the margin, though flipping the seat would still require an extraordinary shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Johnson, the Republican incumbent and Speaker of the House, seeks another term in a northwestern Louisiana district that leans Republican by about 17 points. He has raised roughly $21 million and holds $9.6 million on hand, while Democrats Matt Gromlich and Conrad Cable have each raised under $300,000 with little cash remaining. No public polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

Prediction markets give Johnson about a 94% chance of winning, consistent with the district's strong Republican lean and his elevated national profile. The underlying fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican margin in the mid-to-high teens. Barring an unforeseen development, the seat is expected to remain safely in Republican hands in November.
